- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.4) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < 0.2) — adjust downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
- Overshoots in early forecast horizon (days 1–5) often occur after sentiment spikes — cap forecast growth to 10–15% above recent mean.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.2x recent 7-day average, reduce by 15–20% unless sentiment is strong.
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment drops sharply 3–5 days before forecast, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for delayed reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon — if sentiment is neutral or negative, cap forecast at 10% below recent 14-day moving average.
